idea-plugin.name: Livy Query Console
idea-plugin.description:
Livy Query Console lets you run Spark, PySpark, and Spark SQL code on a remote cluster via Apache Livy directly from your JetBrains IDE.

It is designed for quick exploration, debugging, and day-to-day data engineering workflows: write a snippet, run it in a Livy interactive session, inspect the output, and iterate — without leaving the IDE.

Key features

  • Livy work file: open a dedicated reusable Livy work surface, route editor selection/current line/whole file into it, and execute snippets without leaving the IDE workflow. The work file follows the bound execution kind (`sql`, `pyspark` / `python`, or fallback plain Spark text) and reuses host-IDE highlighting where available.
  • Result viewer: each run is added as a new tab with:
    • Raw response (full JSON output from Livy)
    • Pretty view (human-readable summary including errors and stack traces)
    • Table view for Spark ASCII tables (e.g. output of df.show())
  • Session logs: view Livy session logs in a separate dialog with refresh, copy, and quick find next/previous.
  • Statements browser: list recent statements in a session, inspect deeper details, copy code, and reopen statement code in a bound Livy work file.
  • Tool Window: a “Livy Sessions” tool window that shows active sessions with refresh/auto-refresh, configurable columns, logs/statements actions, and termination for plugin-managed sessions.
  • Connection profiles: keep multiple named Livy targets with per-profile session kind, resource parameters, verbose connection diagnostics, and session management strategy.
  • Managed sessions: reuse compatible plugin-managed sessions, cap managed session count per profile, and optionally clean up the oldest idle managed session when the limit is reached.
  • Browser-based authentication: for SSO/OAuth2-proxy protected Livy endpoints, open an embedded browser login, capture per-profile session cookies, store them in the IDE Password Safe, and prompt to sign in when API calls look authentication-gated.
  • Local history: recent snippets and the last draft per profile can be restored locally for quick rerun/reuse. This is plain-text local persistence, not notebook or remote session restore.

Typical usage

  1. Open Livy: Open Work File (Tools → Livy) or use the Livy editor/project popup actions.
  2. Choose the connection profile to bind the work file or run action to.
  3. If the endpoint is behind SSO/OAuth2 proxy, use Authenticate via Browser… in Settings → Tools → Livy or follow the sign-in prompt.
  4. Route a selection/current line/whole file into Livy, or use Run Current / Run File inside the work file.
  5. Inspect results, logs, and statements, then iterate.

Note: This plugin requires access to a running Apache Livy server. Authentication/SSL behavior depends on your environment (for corporate/self-signed certificates you may need to add the CA certificate to the JetBrains Runtime trust store).

Current scope: the plugin supports multiple named connection profiles for direct Livy HTTP(S) connectivity and SSO/OAuth2-proxy flows that can be satisfied by reusable browser-session cookies. Existing work files and loaded session views stay bound to the profile snapshot they were opened with. Optional local history stores recent snippets and the last draft per profile in plain text on the local machine only. SQL work files support a narrow semicolon-delimited current-statement heuristic; PySpark/plain Spark work files stay on selection-or-file execution semantics. This is a lightweight execution workflow, not notebook persistence or semantic Spark language tooling. Browser sign-in requires an IDE runtime with embedded browser support and stores captured per-profile session cookies in the IDE Password Safe. Manual auth headers/tokens, Kerberos, and generic OAuth token management outside browser-session cookies are still not implemented.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's new in 1.5.5

  • Livy Sessions profile controls: added direct profile creation, profile-list refresh, and a shortcut to Livy profile settings from the Sessions tool window.
  • Fresh profile selection: the Sessions profile selector now reloads after settings changes, when the panel is shown, and when the combo box is opened.
  • Quality and release hardening: added Sonar/Jacoco wiring, dependency verification metadata, and focused coverage for Livy client, settings migration, models, auth helpers, and work-file routing.
